_note: The first banking nodes in the graph, and the first international standard with national implementations on both sides of the border. Read the two chains together and the shape is the same one SNA 2008 already shows: a standard written in Basel that no legislature voted on, implemented as binding capital rules on Canadian banks, and separately as a weekly balance sheet aggregate in Washington. Note what this slice does NOT do: it does not connect to the rest of the graph. See _dropped.

reports.title: Basel Framework
reports.publisher: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Bank for International Settlements
reports.description: The consolidated international standard for bank capital, liquidity and risk measurement, maintained by the Basel Committee and published by the BIS. Not law anywhere; adopted into binding national rules by member jurisdictions, which is why national capital guidelines carry Basel paragraph numbers in their margins.
reports.cadence_note: Maintained as a living consolidated framework with dated amendments rather than issued editions. Filed as annual for the same reason SNA 2008 is — the enum has no bucket for a standard.

release_schedule.note: The Basel Framework is a continuously maintained online consolidated compilation of Basel Committee standards (bis.org/basel_framework/), not a periodic report. It is updated on a rolling basis whenever the Basel Committee finalizes new standards or amendments (e.g., individual chapters carry their own 'Version effective as of' dates, such as the cryptoasset exposures chapter SCO60 effective 1 January 2026). No fixed annual or periodic release calendar or stated rule for the whole document was found; BIS also maintains a 'time traveller' tool showing already-announced future effective dates for specific chapters, but this is not a fixed recurring publication schedule for the framework as a whole.

reports.title: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) Guideline
reports.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
reports.description: The binding capital rules for Canadian banks, federal credit unions, and federally regulated trust and loan companies. Reissued each year across nine chapters covering the definition of capital, credit risk, operational risk, securitization, counterparty risk and market risk. Determines how much capital every Canadian bank must hold against every exposure.

entries.covers: Final CAR Guideline (2027), effective Nov 1, 2026 / Jan 1, 2027 depending on institution fiscal year-end

release_schedule.note: OSFI finalizes a new dated version of the CAR Guideline annually, typically in September, taking effect the following November 1 (institutions with Oct 31 fiscal year-end) or January 1 (institutions with Dec 31 fiscal year-end). CAR Guideline (2026) was finalized Sept 11, 2025; the draft CAR Guideline (2027) consultation closed Feb 18, 2026, and OSFI has stated it plans to publish the final CAR Guideline (2027) in September 2026. The corpus url field pointing to the '2027' draft guideline page is consistent with this pattern; that page currently shows the draft version pending finalization.

reports.title: Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income (Call Report)
reports.description: The quarterly regulatory filing every US commercial bank must submit, giving a full balance sheet and income statement per institution. The authoritative census of American banking against which higher-frequency estimates are benchmarked.

entries.covers: Call Report for report date September 30, 2026 (Q3 2026), due from institutions without foreign offices
Call Report for report date December 31, 2026 (Q4 2026), due from institutions without foreign offices

release_schedule.rule: Under the FFIEC/FDIC/OCC/Federal Reserve interagency Call Report instructions, banks without foreign offices (FFIEC 041/051 filers) must submit within 30 calendar days after the report (quarter-end) date; banks with foreign offices (FFIEC 031 filers, more than one foreign office) get 35 calendar days. If the calculated due date falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.
release_schedule.note: Call Reports are filed quarterly for report (as-of) dates March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31. The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's bank-supervision page lists explicit deadlines through Q3 2026 (confirmed: Dec 31 2025 report due Fri Jan 30 2026 -- verified directly against FDIC's own FIL for Q4 2025 -- and Sept 30 2026 report due Fri Oct 30 2026). The Q4 2026 entry (Dec 31, 2026 report) was not yet listed on any source as of Aug 2026 (FDIC/FFIEC typically publish the FIL for a quarter only after that quarter closes), so I computed it myself: 30 days after Dec 31, 2026 is Jan 30, 2027, which falls on a Saturday, so under the standard weekend-rollover rule the deadline would move to Monday, Feb 1, 2027 -- this specific date is my computation (implied), not yet published by the agencies. The Q2 2026 report (June 30, 2026) was already due July 30, 2026, which is in the past relative to 2026-08-11, so it is omitted.

reports.title: Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks in the United States (H.8)
reports.description: Weekly estimated aggregate balance sheet for all US commercial banks, published each Friday afternoon. The Federal Reserve's oldest data collection, originating in the needs of the First World War, and the highest-frequency read on bank credit conditions available anywhere.

entries.covers: H.8 weekly data through the week ending August 12, 2026

release_schedule.rule: Published weekly, the release is typically available to the public by 4:15 p.m. each Friday. If Friday is a federal holiday, then the data are released on Thursday.
release_schedule.note: Confirmed against current page: release dated August 7, 2026 (Friday) was the latest as of today (2026-08-11); next scheduled Friday is August 14, 2026, no federal holiday intervening. Weekly cadence (52/yr) already on file matches this rule.

reports.title: Capital Adequacy of Bank Holding Companies, Savings and Loan Holding Companies, and State Member Banks (Regulation Q), 12 CFR part 217
reports.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
reports.description: The binding regulatory capital rules for US bank holding companies, savings and loan holding companies and state member banks -- the American counterpart to `osfi-car-guideline`, and the node the US half of the Basel chain was missing. eCFR gives the part's official title as "Capital Adequacy of Bank Holding Companies, Savings and Loan Holding Companies, and State Member Banks (Regulation Q)" and s.217.1(a) as "This part establishes minimum capital requirements and overall capital adequacy standards for entities described in paragraph (c)(1)...". Adopted by the Board and the OCC as a joint final rule published 11 October 2013 (FR doc. 2013-21653), whose own title is "Regulatory Capital Rules: Regulatory Capital, Implementation of Basel III, Capital Adequacy, Transition Provisions, Prompt Corrective Action, Standardized Approach for Risk-weighted Assets, Market Discipline and Disclosure Requirements, Advanced Approaches Risk-Based Capital Rule, and Market Risk Capital Rule". Note the asymmetry with the Canadian side that makes this pair worth having: OSFI reissues a guideline annually and prints Basel paragraph numbers in the margins; the Federal Reserve codified Basel III once into a CFR part and amends it. Same standard, two different instruments of adoption. MINTED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass) on the one-off foundational-instrument shape of `Research.1.md` sec.4 -- government regulation, named and titled -- so `releases_per_year` is deliberately absent, as with `eu-reg-2016-2304`. eCFR showed the part as last amended 27 November 2023 at the time of this read; amendments within the one codified generation are not treated as a cadence, per sec.4's recast paragraph.

dependencies.basis: Chapter 1 states it directly: 'This chapter is drawn from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel Framework published on the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) website.' The dependency is visible on almost every page — individual requirements carry their Basel paragraph number in square brackets, so 'RBC 20.4' sits at the end of a rule binding on Canadian banks.

'The H.8 estimates are primarily based on the FR 2644 reporting form ... and quarterly Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income (Call Reports) for those commercial banks that are not included in the FR 2644 panel.' The large-bank panel is defined by ranking 'based on the commercial bank Call Reports to which the H.8 release data had been most recently benchmarked' — the weekly estimate is a sample tethered to the quarterly census.

reference_period.stated_as: The weekly H.8 sample is tethered to the 'quarterly Consolidated Reports of Condition and Income', against which it is benchmarked.
